destination_record.name: Andaman & Nicobar
destination_record.tagline: Clear turquoise water, white-sand beaches and the history of Cellular Jail, on India's island chain in the Bay of Bengal.
destination_record.places: Port Blair, Cellular Jail, Ross Island, North Bay, Havelock (Swaraj Dweep), Radhanagar Beach, Elephant Beach, Neil Island (Shaheed Dweep), Bharatpur Beach, Baratang, Chidiya Tapu

on.places: Havelock (Swaraj Dweep), Neil (Shaheed Dweep), Port Blair, Ross Island, North Bay
on.activities: Scuba diving, snorkelling at Elephant Beach and North Bay, glass-bottom boat rides, beach days at Radhanagar and island-hopping by ferry. Seas are generally calmest and visibility best from December to March. Days turn hot by April, and peak dates around Christmas and New Year book out early.

mid.places: Port Blair, Cellular Jail, Ross Island, Havelock beaches in dry spells
mid.activities: Showers, humid heat and changing sea conditions. Ferries and water activities can be delayed or cancelled at short notice, so keep your plans flexible. Rates are lower than in the main season.

off.places: Port Blair museums and Cellular Jail, with limited island sightseeing
off.activities: South-west monsoon with heavy rain and rough seas. Ferries can be suspended and diving and water sports are often limited. The islands are lush and green and rates are lowest, but we advise this season only for flexible travellers.

profile.overview:
The Andaman Islands lie in the Bay of Bengal, much nearer to Myanmar and Thailand than to the Indian mainland, yet they are part of India. Radhanagar Beach on Havelock is one of the country's most celebrated stretches of sand, the water is clear enough for snorkelling close to shore, and the coral reefs make this one of the easiest places in India to try scuba diving. Port Blair adds history, with Cellular Jail where freedom fighters were imprisoned and the colonial ruins of Ross Island.

Most visitors fly into Port Blair and take ferries to Havelock (Swaraj Dweep) and Neil (Shaheed Dweep), where days pass in beach time, snorkelling and unhurried sunsets. Indian citizens need no passport or visa, which makes it an easy first island holiday. Ferries depend on the sea, so we plan with sensible buffers and keep the weather in mind throughout.

facts.capital: Port Blair (renamed Sri Vijaya Puram), capital of the Union Territory
facts.languages: Hindi and English, with Bengali, Tamil and Telugu widely spoken
facts.climate: About 24°C to 32°C all year, humid; south-west monsoon from June to September and showers in October and November
facts.flight_time: Fly into Port Blair (IXZ): about 2 hr from Chennai or Kolkata and about 4 hr from Delhi. There is no rail link.

reasons.title: Beaches among the best in India
reasons.text: Radhanagar, Elephant Beach and Bharatpur have soft white sand and clear, calm water that is easy to swim and snorkel in.

reasons.title: Easy first scuba dive
reasons.text: Discover Scuba sessions with certified instructors let beginners see coral and reef fish without any prior training.

reasons.title: History with meaning
reasons.text: Cellular Jail and its evening Light and Sound show tell the story of India's freedom struggle in a moving setting.

reasons.title: No visa or passport
reasons.text: Indian citizens travel on a valid photo ID, so the trip is as simple as a domestic holiday, though it feels like a world away.

reasons.title: Slow, uncrowded islands
reasons.text: Havelock and Neil keep a quiet pace, with beach shacks, cycle rides and sunsets rather than crowds and traffic.

attractions.title: Cellular Jail, Port Blair
attractions.text: A colonial-era prison turned national memorial, with an evening Light and Sound show about the freedom fighters held here.

attractions.title: Radhanagar Beach, Havelock
attractions.text: A long, curving white beach backed by forest, famous for its sunsets and safe, shallow swimming.

attractions.title: Elephant Beach, Havelock
attractions.text: Reached by a short boat ride, with shallow reef for snorkelling and glass-bottom boat trips.

attractions.title: Ross Island
attractions.text: The former British administrative headquarters, now a quiet island of ruined bungalows, a church and roaming deer.

attractions.title: Bharatpur Beach and Natural Bridge, Neil
attractions.text: Calm shallows for snorkelling and a rock arch formed by the sea, best seen at low tide.

attractions.title: North Bay, Port Blair
attractions.text: A coral beach near Port Blair for snorkelling, glass-bottom boats and sea walks, reached by boat.

attractions.title: Baratang limestone caves
attractions.text: A long day trip by road and boat through mangrove creeks to natural limestone formations.

attractions.title: Chidiya Tapu
attractions.text: A quiet southern tip of South Andaman, known for sunsets and birdwatching.

experiences.title: Discover Scuba at Havelock
experiences.text: A beginner dive with a certified instructor, subject to medical fitness and sea conditions.

experiences.title: Snorkelling on the reef
experiences.text: Shallow coral and reef fish at Elephant Beach, North Bay and Bharatpur, with visibility depending on tides and weather.

experiences.title: Sea walk at North Bay
experiences.text: Walk on the seabed in a helmet with an instructor, no swimming needed. Available as an optional activity.

experiences.title: Glass-bottom boat rides
experiences.text: A good way for families and older travellers to see coral without getting into the water.

experiences.title: Sunset at Radhanagar or Laxmanpur
experiences.text: Walk onto the sand in the late afternoon and watch the sky change colour over the Bay of Bengal.

experiences.title: Cellular Jail Light and Sound show
experiences.text: An evening show that tells the story of the jail and the people held there.

food.title: Fresh seafood
food.text: Grilled fish, prawns, crab and fish curry are on most menus. Ask what was landed that day.

food.title: Bengali and South Indian meals
food.text: Settler communities from the mainland have made fish curry with rice, dosas and thalis easy to find in Port Blair.

food.title: Tender coconut
food.text: Sold at beaches and roadside stalls, and a welcome cool drink after a day in the sun.

food.title: Vegetarian and Jain meals
food.text: Available at many restaurants in Port Blair and Havelock. Choice is narrower on Neil, so tell us in advance and we will plan around it.

tips.title: Book early and expect ferry changes
tips.text: Ferries between islands run on the sea's terms and can be delayed or cancelled. Keep a buffer before flying home.

tips.title: Carry cash
tips.text: ATMs are limited and sometimes out of cash on Havelock and Neil, and card or UPI payments depend on patchy networks.

tips.title: Do not collect shells or coral
tips.text: Removing coral, shells and sand from the islands is prohibited, so leave them where they are.

tips.title: Respect tribal reserves
tips.text: Some areas, including the Jarawa reserve on the Baratang road, have strict rules against stopping, photography and contact.

tips.title: Plan scuba early in the stay
tips.text: Avoid flying for at least 24 hours after a scuba dive, so schedule dives well before your departure day.

tips.title: Expect limited mobile coverage
tips.text: Networks and internet can be slow or absent on the smaller islands, so download maps and tickets before you go.

travel_info.visa: Indian citizens need no visa or passport for the Andaman Islands. Carry a valid government photo ID such as an Aadhaar card, passport, voter ID or driving licence, which is checked for flights and ferries. The tourist islands in our packages, including Port Blair, Havelock and Neil, need no separate permit for Indian citizens, but tribal reserves and the Nicobar group are restricted. We arrange permits and confirm the current rules at booking.
travel_info.health: No compulsory vaccinations from the mainland. Carry sunscreen, insect repellent, any regular medicines and a basic first-aid kit, as medical facilities on Havelock and Neil are limited. Scuba diving needs a medical declaration, and you should avoid flying for at least 24 hours after a dive. Take care with sea currents and coral cuts.
travel_info.money: Take enough cash for the smaller islands, as ATMs can be out of order or empty and card or UPI payments rely on patchy networks. Port Blair has the most banks and ATMs. Tips are optional for drivers and guides.

faqs.q: How many days do I need for the Andaman Islands?
faqs.a: Five to six nights is comfortable for Port Blair, Havelock and Neil. A shorter weekend trip can cover Port Blair and Havelock, and seven nights lets you add Baratang and more beach time.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit?
faqs.a: November to April is the main season, with calmer seas and better visibility, especially from December to March. June to September is the south-west monsoon, when ferries and water activities can be limited.

faqs.q: How do we reach the Andaman Islands?
faqs.a: Most travellers fly into Port Blair (IXZ) from Chennai, Kolkata or Delhi. Ferries from the mainland also run but take days. Transfers between Port Blair, Havelock and Neil are by ferry, which depends on the weather.

faqs.q: Can I enjoy the islands without scuba diving?
faqs.a: Yes. Many visitors spend their time on the beaches, on glass-bottom boats and snorkelling, and visiting Cellular Jail and Ross Island. Scuba is optional and suited to beginners with instructors.

faqs.q: Is the trip suitable for senior parents and children?
faqs.a: Yes, with a relaxed itinerary. Ferry crossings and some beach access involve steps and walking, so tell us about mobility needs and we can base you longer in fewer places.

faqs.q: What if the ferry is cancelled?
faqs.a: Ferries can be delayed or cancelled in rough weather. We rearrange the order of the programme where possible and advise a buffer day or a late flight on the last day. Costs of extra nights caused by weather are not included.

group_trips.title: Port Blair, Havelock and Neil Island Group Trip
group_trips.summary: Seven days across the Andaman Islands with Cellular Jail, Ross Island, Radhanagar and Elephant Beach, and Neil's quiet shores, travelling in a small group.
group_trips.overview:
This group trip covers the classic Andaman circuit over six nights: two in Port Blair, two in Havelock (Swaraj Dweep), one in Neil Island (Shaheed Dweep) and a final night back in Port Blair. You visit Cellular Jail and its evening Light and Sound show, explore Ross Island and North Bay, and spend time on Radhanagar Beach and Elephant Beach.

Ferries link the islands, and sailing times depend on the sea, so the order of days may change on the day. A trip captain travels with the group throughout, and Indian meal options are available on request.

The pace is easy, with free time on most days. Snorkelling is optional and diving can be added on request, which suits families, friends travelling together and senior parents.

honeymoon_trips.title: Andaman Honeymoon: Island Sunsets, Beach Dinner and Private Car Days
honeymoon_trips.summary: Six unhurried nights for two across Port Blair, Havelock and Neil, with Radhanagar Beach sunsets, a couples spa session and a candlelight dinner by the sea.
honeymoon_trips.overview:
This private honeymoon moves at an easy pace: one night in Port Blair, three in Havelock (Swaraj Dweep), one in Neil Island (Shaheed Dweep) and a final night in Port Blair. You travel by private car on each island and take ferries between them, with later starts and nothing packed into a single day.

Havelock is the heart of the trip, with Radhanagar Beach at sunset, a boat outing to Elephant Beach and time to simply be together. Neil adds Bharatpur Beach, the Natural Bridge and the golden light of Laxmanpur.

Expect a flower welcome, a couples spa session and a candlelight dinner by the beach, all subject to availability. Tell us your wedding date at booking so the hotels can prepare.

custom_trips.title: Andaman Family Holiday: Port Blair and Havelock
custom_trips.summary: Six easy days for families with Corbyn's Cove, Cellular Jail, Ross Island, North Bay and two nights on Havelock's Radhanagar and Elephant beaches.
custom_trips.overview:
This private family holiday uses two bases, Port Blair and Havelock (Swaraj Dweep), so there is only one ferry each way and little repacking. In Port Blair you visit a calm beach, Cellular Jail, Ross Island and North Bay, where glass-bottom boats let children see coral without swimming.

On Havelock you spend time at Radhanagar Beach and take a boat to Elephant Beach. The pace is relaxed, with free time each day, which suits children and grandparents. We can adjust meals and activities to the group's needs.
